name: Cut and Stick
description: Baby Ehab has a piece of Cut and Stick with an array $$$a$$$ of length $$$n$$$ written on it. He plans to grab a pair of scissors and do the following to it: pick a range $$$(l, r)$$$ and cut out every element $$$a_l$$$, $$$a_{l + 1}$$$, ..., $$$a_r$$$ in this range; stick some of the elements together in the same order they were in the array; end up with multiple pieces, where every piece contains some of the elements and every element belongs to some piece. More formally, he partitions the sequence $$$a_l$$$, $$$a_{l + 1}$$$, ..., $$$a_r$$$ into subsequences. He thinks a partitioning is beautiful if for every piece (subsequence) it holds that, if it has length $$$x$$$, then no value occurs strictly more than $$$\lceil \frac{x}{2} \rceil$$$ times in it. He didn't pick a range yet, so he's wondering: for $$$q$$$ ranges $$$(l, r)$$$, what is the minimum number of pieces he needs to partition the elements $$$a_l$$$, $$$a_{l + 1}$$$, ..., $$$a_r$$$ into so that the partitioning is beautiful. A sequence $$$b$$$ is a subsequence of an array $$$a$$$ if $$$b$$$ can be obtained from $$$a$$$ by deleting some (possibly zero) elements. Note that it does not have to be contiguous.
input_specification: The first line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$q$$$ ($$$1 \le n,q \le 3 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the length of the array $$$a$$$ and the number of queries. The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1$$$, $$$a_2$$$, ..., $$$a_{n}$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le n$$$) — the elements of the array $$$a$$$. Each of the next $$$q$$$ lines contains two integers $$$l$$$ and $$$r$$$ ($$$1 \le l \le r \le n$$$) — the range of this query.
output_specification: For each query, print the minimum number of subsequences you need to partition this range into so that the partitioning is beautiful. We can prove such partitioning always exists.
approach_summary: Build a Segment Tree over the array. Implement point update and associative range query operations in O(log N) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1514D — Cut and Stick [57. Segment Tree (Point Update Range Query)]
topic_editorial.summary: Range queries and updates via Segment Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The query operation is associative (e.g., sum, min, max, gcd). Any contiguous range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into at most $O(\log N)$ canonical dyadic intervals represented by nodes in a binary tree.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Tree Construction
We build a binary segment tree over array $A[1..N]$.
Each node covers a segment $[L, R]$. If $L = R$, the node stores $A[L]$. Otherwise:
$$\text{node.val} = \text{combine}(\text{left\_child.val}, \text{right\_child.val})$$

### Step 2: Point / Range Updates
To update position $pos$ with value $val$:
- Traverse down to the leaf node $[pos, pos]$.
- Update leaf value.
- Recompute ancestor values on the way back up in $O(\log N)$ time.

### Step 3: Range Query Processing
To query the associative aggregate on range $[qL, qR]$:
- If current segment $[L, R]$ is completely within $[qL, qR]$, return node value.
- If disjoint, return identity element.
- Otherwise, split and return $\text{combine}(\text{query}(left), \text{query}(right))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((N + Q) \log N)$
  Building the segment tree takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Each point/range query and update traverses at most $4 \log N$ tree nodes, requiring $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ time per query.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  A standard binary segment tree requires at most $4N$ nodes to represent elements up to index $N$.
